stop_reason: Max iterations (2) reached. The candidate pool is substantively sufficient for the collection workflow to proceed with PAHO, UNICEF, WHO, and ReliefWeb sources covering most of 2024. Three unresolved gaps (MSPP direct bulletins, post-March 2024 PAHO joint reports, individual UNICEF 2024 monthly SitRep content) are documented as unexecuted follow-up queries for human review or a future extended search run.
final_coverage_assessment: Temporal coverage: PAHO Situation Report 8 (13 March 2024) and PAHO epidemiological update (26 April 2024) confirm Q1 2024 coverage. The UNICEF SitRep index snippet explicitly lists monthly reports from January–February 2024 through November 2024, providing a near-complete 2024 temporal chain. Post-March 2024 PAHO joint humanitarian/cholera reports are referenced but not individually surfaced. December 2024 is not explicitly confirmed in any accepted candidate. Geographic coverage: National-level Haiti data is well-covered. Subnational (department-level) data is not confirmed in any accepted snippet — MSPP bulletins (the primary subnational source) were not retrieved. Field coverage: cases_suspected, deaths, and date_reported are likely present in PAHO and UNICEF documents. cases_confirmed, hospitalizations, and subnational_location fields remain uncertain without MSPP or individual UNICEF SitRep content.
final_trustworthiness_assessment: High-trust sources dominate the accepted candidate pool: paho.org (5 results), who.int (3), unicef.org (3), reliefweb.int (2), gtfcc.org (1). These are all authoritative international public health or humanitarian organizations. BEACON (beaconbio.org) is a credible academic disease surveillance aggregator (Boston University/HealthMap). The haitiantimes.com result has garbled date references (mixing 2022, 2025 dates in the same snippet) and should be flagged for human review before use as evidence. The MSPP absence is a trust gap — national authority data would be the gold standard for subnational figures.
